Then followed Kemp and Galloway, of S.W.C., with Ted Saunders fourth. Final scores appear below, and it will be seen that our hosts were winners by 56 points to 80.
Churcher was an individual entrant, and our team was completed by Ted Saunders, and gained a narrow two-point victory over our Enfield rivals.
Our President started the race and Tommy Green, the holder; Fred Rickards, a past holder; Harold King, and Len Fletcher were soon in the lead closely followed by Ted Saunders.

Second place was taken by Don Brown, still improving and likely to improve still further into the very top class; and Ted Saunders, always persevering and likely to be a valuable aid to the Club at twenty miles, took the third medal.
Fifth for us came Ted Saunders in the 29th position. As usual, he started very slowly, and at 10 miles was still back in the fifties or sixties.

Ted Saunders finished 13th (2 hr. 53 min. 21 sec.)—a sound walk. Despite the travelling difficulties encountered on Boxing Day, and the rather more obvious handicap the festival season imposes, it should be possible for us to enter a much larger number, and it to be hoped that this will be the case…

If Ted Saunders had not been indisposed the previous week, and had been able to reproduce his running in the Middlesex Championship, we should probably have taken a place; but as it is, this must be deferred for another year.

Our readers will be sorry to learn of the indisposition of Ted Saunders, a Vice-Captain and prominent walker for many years past. All Belgravians will wish him a speedy recovery to normal health, and we all hope to see him fit and well in our company in the near future.

Of our other one-time invalids, Ted Saunders is out walking with us again, and Harry Shields has made a marvellously quick recovery from his recent operation, and will probably be running again over the country before you read these notes.
Roberts, competing in his first big race for us, was 44th, Harley 57th and Ted Saunders 68th. Frank Elson was compelled to retire from the race.
Reeve, is in the R.A.O.C.; whilst Ted Saunders is a corporal in an R.A.M.C. unit functioning in the Near East.
